There are men and women in the world who suffer from wind-stroke, or are crippled by exhaustion, or are blind, deaf, or mute;
or whose bodies are entangled in illness for years and months, lying prostrate upon their beds, unable to rise as death approaches.

When their breath ceases, their spirits are summoned into the Office of the Shades (*yinsi*), where the evils they have committed in past lives and in this life are examined, along with the causes, conditions, and karmic retributions, down to the finest detail.

There is no difference. If one offers the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, whether copying it oneself or for others, or upholding it throughout one's life, as soon as one raises the mind or stirs a thought, the officials of the underworld will be confused;
while they are inspecting one's meritorious deeds, they will first release the soul and spirit to possess the body.
Subsequently, he encountered a skilled physician, and his illness was immediately cured. Upon waking, he attained spiritual awakening.

The following morning, he had his wife burn incense and, personally before the various Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, made a solemn vow to offer one thousand scrolls of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* and, furthermore, to maintain its recitation for the remainder of his life.
Thereafter, he again dreamed that a Vajra deity bestowed medicine upon him.
He gave him a single pill and instructed Chengxin to swallow it. On the following day, his illness was immediately cured. After nursing him for over a month, his body became light and robust;

both his appearance and spirit were fully restored to their former state. All who saw or heard of this joined their palms in praise, saying that this sutra possesses the power to raise the dead back to life.
How could one not be cautious and reverent toward it?

Tang Zhen of the Song dynasty was a jailer in Kuaiji County, Xingzhou Prefecture. He regularly recited three fascicles of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* every day, never flagging regardless of cold or heat.
In the eighth year of the Shaoxing era, he colluded with Zhu Xun and Zhu Mao to embezzle official funds. When the matter was discovered—
The case was reported from the county to the prefecture. Lord Zhao issued a decree to send it to the Judicial Court for re-examination.

When Tang Zhen and the others arrived, he had a dream at night in which a Vajra deity spoke to him, saying: "Because you have maintained the recitation of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* throughout your life, you have moved the divine response;
you need only set your mind at ease. At the time of the final judgment, I shall assist the Lord with my divine brush to first issue the verdict."

The ten officials were each sentenced to one hundred strokes of the backstaff and banished to neighboring prefectures. You, however, were sentenced to one hundred strokes of the backstaff and returned to prison custody;

you shall be released upon the recovery of the full amount of the stolen goods and sent back home. Upon waking, he reflected on this again and again: "Since I am the leader, the nature of the offense we committed is the same;
how can there be such a difference in the severity of our punishments? This is truly incomprehensible. Thus it was, until the time of his final sentencing. He was then led away one by one.
The single fruit corresponded to his dream without the slightest discrepancy.
Those who saw and heard of this were all struck by its wonder, and only then did they realize that the merit of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā* possesses inconceivable power.

Thus, moved by the spiritual power of the *Vajra*, it secretly assisted the brush of Minister Zhao; how could there be any further doubt? Thereafter, he made a vow to print and distribute the [sutra].
He devoted himself exclusively for his entire life to the study, recitation, and upholding of the three hundred fascicles of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
He lived to the age of eighty-five and passed away without illness (as recorded in the *Zazu ji*).
In the ninth year of the Shaoxing era of the Song dynasty, there was a woman of the Wang family from Mingzhou who regularly recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
She accompanied her husband to his post in Qizhou; she had been pregnant for twenty-eight months but was unable to give birth. Furthermore, because she had [recited] too much...
She was ill; her physical frame was emaciated. She harbored deep anxieties that at the time of childbirth, both mother and child might not survive. Her distress was unceasing.
One day, as she stood leaning against the door, she happened to see a strange monk who exhorted her, saying, "Together we shall increase our merit and blessings.
After Lady Wang had offered money in alms, the monk said, "Madam, you possess roots of goodness. Why do you not print and distribute the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*? If you were to..."
By printing and distributing one thousand copies of the *Heart Sūtra*, one shall increase their blessings and longevity in this life; parents, children, and grandchildren shall remain united;
all wishes shall be fulfilled; and merit shall extend to the seven generations of ancestors and all deceased relatives, who shall all attain transcendence.

Wang Shi was deeply awakened and, following the monk’s instructions, subsequently printed and distributed one thousand copies of the *Diamond Sūtra* and provided a vegetarian feast for one thousand monks.

She then recited one thousand scrolls of sutras and personally went to Tianning Temple to perform repentance before the Triple Gem, praying for protection and blessings on the day of her delivery so that both mother and child might be safe and sound.
Before long, her prayers were answered. After the fast, she returned home;
at the third watch of the night, she had a dream in which she saw a golden Vajrapāṇi deity pointing a mallet toward Lady Wang’s abdomen, causing such unbearable pain that she could not endure it.
Upon awakening, she found two boys lying on the bed, their features perfectly formed and so lovely as to bring joy to all who beheld them.
Relying solely upon the power of Prajñā and protected by celestial deities, the response was swift; thus, Lady Wang’s mother and both sons were preserved whole.
Overwhelmed with joy and gratitude, she thereafter devoted herself single-mindedly to pure conduct, reciting the sutras without ceasing until she reached the age of sixty-one. No...
Suddenly, she passed away. She saw two messengers lead her before the Son of Heaven, Yama, who commanded, "What good deeds did you perform while alive?
Lady Wang replied, "Since my youth, I have maintained the recitation of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, not missing a single day until now.
The Son of Heaven granted Lady Wang a golden throne, and she sat beside the hall, chanting it aloud.
Throughout [the realms], the bitter sufferings of hell were instantly stilled. All those undergoing retribution in hell universally received the benefit of this grace.
The Son of Heaven questioned Wang Shi again, asking, "Why did you not recite the mantra? He replied, "There was no original text in the world.

An imperial edict was issued ordering the ghost-officials to retrieve the original mantra from the treasury and deliver it to Wang Shi. They were instructed, saying: "When you return to the world of the living, circulate it widely and ensure its transmission. Be diligent!

"Do not let this be lost or forgotten. The Son of Heaven further said, "When the Wang family reaches the end of their lives hereafter, they shall go directly to the World of Ultimate Bliss and shall never return to this place again."
The mantra for supplementing deficiencies is: Oṃ hulu hulu śaye ke svāhā.
One directs [the merit] toward the suchness of the ultimate reality (bhūtakoṭi), with mind and mind in perfect accord.
Second, dedicating [merit] toward the unsurpassed fruit of Buddhahood so that it is perfected in every moment;
third, dedicating [merit] so that all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm may together be born in the Pure Land.
— By the Licentiate Zhu.

During the Song Dynasty, there was a Zhu, a Jinshi (presented scholar) from Suzhou Prefecture. He wore the robes and caps of a Confucian scholar and devoted himself to the studies for the civil service examinations;
throughout his life, he had never known the subtlety of the Buddha-dharma. One day, while wandering at leisure, he happened to visit Tiger Hill Monastery (*Hǔqīu Sì*).

It coincided with the time when Chan Master Foyin was lecturing on the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, reaching the passage: "All conditioned phenomena are like a dream, an illusion, a bubble, and a shadow; they are like dew..."
"It is also like lightning; one should contemplate it in this way. The Master explained the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma point by point. Upon hearing this, Zhu was greatly delighted.
He thought to himself, "In my daily life, I have never heard such teachings on the Buddha-dharma; they are profoundly reasonable. He regretted that his life had not been fulfilled.
Joyfully returning home, he suddenly fell asleep at noon the following day. He dreamed of a ghost official escorting five criminals, with Zhu following behind them.
After traveling about two li, they came upon a major street and entered a lane; there was a house with a blue cloth curtain hanging at its entrance.
The ghost official lifted the curtain, and the criminals all went inside. Upon reaching the kitchen, they saw a bucket of hot water on the hearth.
The sinners all went away to eat. Zhu also felt thirsty and was just about to drink when he was stopped by a ghost official who shouted, "Those who listen to the Buddha-dharma must not drink.
Startled by this, he woke up; his mind remained suspicious of the dream, so he walked at a steady pace until he reached the main street.
He entered an alleyway. Indeed, there was a house that was no different from the one in his dream. Zhu knocked on the door and went inside.
When the master of the house saw the Jinshi arrive, he hurriedly came forward to greet him. Zhu asked, "Just now, what news was there in your residence's kitchen?
The master then questioned his family members, who said, "Below the kitchen, we have been raising six small dogs; one of them has died."

Zhu was immediately struck with alarm and broke into a sweat. He thought to himself, "If I had not heard the power of the Buddha-dharma, I would have entered the womb of a dog and been transformed into a beast.
Thereupon, he abandoned his former habits and devoted himself single-mindedly to reciting the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Without ceasing through cold or heat, his life reached eighty-nine years.
When his meritorious practice was perfected, on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, he invited all the masters, virtuous friends, and kinsmen from the various mountains to see him off.
He then ascended to the tips of the branches in the rear garden, recited a four-line verse to part from the assembly, and stood upright, passing away into nirvana. The verse says: "Eighty..."
In the ninth year, Master Zhu split the void with both hands and trod upon the floating clouds until they were pulverized; he then manifested his transformation to the east of the Bodhi tree.
— Yang Yan.

On the thirteenth day of the third month in the seventh year of the Qiandao era of the Song dynasty, Yang Yan—the son of Wang Hui, who held the rank of Left Zhongtaifu, was a Palace Attendant of the Longtu Pavilion, and served as the Director of the Youshen Observation—suddenly dreamed that his father, Wang Hui, was together with his mother, the Lady.
The Longtu Pavilion official recalled that his parents had already abandoned their orphaned children; fearing they might depart too soon, he earnestly entreated them to remain for ten months.
Lòng-đồ apologized, and Prince Hwang accepted his request. Lòng-đồ bowed twice and offered wine according to the ritual of treating a living person with courtesy.
Lòng-đồ wept; Prince Hwang and his consort also wept. Lòng-đồ asked Prince Hwang about the merits he had habitually cultivated:

"May the offerings of money and goods I have burned be of use? Prince Hwang replied, "They are of use. He asked again, "Between the fruits of merit from the Buddhist and Daoist paths, which is superior?"
"Excellent. Wang Yun said, "One day, simply raise your hand and turn it over. The Dragon asked again, "Among the scriptures of the world, which is the most excellent?
Wang Yun replied, "The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* is held in the deepest reverence by the courts of the underworld.

If you were to have me print and distribute one thousand copies for its sake, that would be the very best. The Dragon, intending to provide funeral implements for the afterlife, immediately responded.
Yunrong said, "I shall fashion it to present to you. Prince Wang said, "Very well.

At that time, as evening fell, suddenly a swift-footed messenger came walking across the water, reporting that at the hour of You (5–7 p.m.), a golden tablet had passed through Chuzhou. Longtu addressed him again, asking, "Where is Your Highness now?
Prince Wang said, "I am currently presiding over the Earth Department. While they were still lingering in conversation, he suddenly woke from his sleep.
Overwhelmed by grief, he shed tears upon his pillow and mat. He then thought of General Wang’s heroic spirit, which remained unclouded; his countenance appeared as if he were still alive.
Indeed, General Wang had been a great general of the Song dynasty, who through a hundred battles quelled calamities and unrest.

His great achievements were manifold; he captured enemies without killing them, sparing a vast number of lives. He served at the imperial court for nearly forty years, never having executed a single person unjustly. His loyalty—
Be magnanimous and forgiving; you shall surely receive the assistance of merit and virtue. Having a presiding authority, you may observe the merits cultivated by those among the living.

When the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* is recited, the funerary offerings burned for the deceased will all be utilized in the underworld. Furthermore, one comes to know the retribution for good and evil;
the realms of the dead and the living are of one essence, with no distinction between this side and that. This is sufficient to exhort the world toward doing good.

...is [the one who] did so. On the day of the birth of Śākyamuni Buddha, Longtu respectfully witnessed [him] establish a single great assembly of the Water and Land *zhai* for the spirits of heaven and earth and the living and the dead at Chanfuzi Temple, as well as providing offerings for several monks.

He performed the ritual according to the Dharma, reciting the *Jinguangming Sande Miaochan* (The Wondrous Repentance of the Three Virtues of the Golden Light) for seven days and nights, and commanded the monastic community to chant the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*.
One collection of the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, totaling five thousand forty-eight fascicles, was used to provide merit for the posthumous well-being of his two parents.
Prepared by Zhou Xing of the Chengju Bureau.

In the first year of the Chunxi era of the Song dynasty, Zhou Xing, a local official (*chengju*) of Yangzhou Prefecture, had recited one scroll of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* daily since childhood.
He never wavered in his resolve, whether in public or private affairs.

Once, he was commissioned by the Prefect, Lord Mo, to carry a gift of coarse silk, incense, candles, and birthday offerings totaling approximately one thousand *guan* to present to high-ranking court officials on their birthdays at the imperial capital. While traveling, he reached Gua...

The three brothers, the Yūs, were staying at a guesthouse by the ferry crossing. When the couple saw that the official’s luggage contained heavy goods, they called for their elder brother, Yūji, to plot and deliberate.
At the third watch of the night, they entered the room and secretly beat Zhou Xing to death.
About five *li* from the inn, he was buried by the roadside. His luggage and property had all been plundered.

Because the local office exceeded its deadline for reporting, the official dispatches were delayed and prolonged, leaving him with no means of returning home. His wife and children were twice detained by the authorities and subjected to corporal punishment under legal restrictions;
a full year has now passed, making their recovery truly difficult. Subsequently, because the Prefectural Governor was summoned to the imperial court, one—
As the traveler set out on his journey and had not yet reached the Guazhou ferry—when he was still about five li away—a single lotus flower suddenly appeared blocking the road.
The Governor ordered his attendants to break it off, but even with their knives they could not sever it.
They then dug down four or five feet and discovered a dead man; the lotus flower was emerging from his mouth. The crowd marveled at this miraculous protection.
He was taken out. When looked at closely, his eyes were still moving. After being gazed upon repeatedly and scrutinized for some time, it was revealed to be Zhou the Clerk.
He was brought to a private residence and nursed slowly with gruel; only on the following day was he able to speak. He said, "I was robbed to death by the innkeepers Yu and the others.
I have been buried in the ground for sixteen months already. The Prefect asked in astonishment, "How did you come back to life?"

Furthermore, he did not feel hunger. He replied, "By the power of reciting the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* every day, while I was buried in the ground as if in a dream, I saw a Vajra deity who inserted a lotus flower into Zhou Xing’s mouth;
henceforth, I have felt neither hunger nor thirst. The Prefect joined his palms and praised him, saying, "I have often heard that this sutra possesses inconceivable [power]."
Reflecting upon these merits, I am filled with self-reproach for having imprisoned Zhou Xing’s wife and children for so many years; what regret can now avail?

Furthermore, among the legal cases I have handled in my daily duties, there were undoubtedly instances of injustice. I have therefore issued a formal dispatch to the Magistrate of Yangzhou, requesting that he immediately release Zhou Xing’s family.
I have also dispatched messengers at once to arrest Yu Er, Yu San, their wives, and others, in order to interrogate them.

The facts were made clear. Yu Er and the others confessed and submitted themselves, stating that they had beaten Zhou Xing to death and seized ten rolls of brocade, a block of agarwood, ten longevity candles, along with various items for a birthday offering. This account was recorded in detail and reported to the throne.

The Emperor issued an edict, deliberating that because Zhou Xing had upheld the merit and power of the Buddha-dharma, he was protected by gods and spirits; thus, he has now been restored to life. As for Yu...
The two plots and three conspiracies were crimes of truly grave nature. Had their lives been spared, there was concern they might again plot in secret to harm others;
therefore, they were all sentenced to death by severe flogging. Their wives were each given twenty strokes across the spine and exiled to military prefectures overseas, never to be released.
Since good deeds have their retribution, so too do evil ones. How could one not take this as a warning? (From the *Zazujiji*).
Guo Chengsi, a resident of Shaoxing Prefecture who has been newly appointed as a Military Aide (Canjun) to Wenzhou, was about to depart for his post.
He personally visited the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas at Tianning Temple and, burning incense, made this vow: "I shall take my family of nine members to take up my post in Wenzhou."
I make these vows: First, upon arriving at my post, may the entire family refrain from eating beef.

Second, while holding authority and administering government affairs, may I always practice skillful means, showing compassion to the orphaned and the poor, relieving others' urgent needs, and rescuing them from peril.

Upon completing my term of office and returning home, I vow to donate funds to have one scroll of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* transcribed, which shall be respectfully enshrined in a Buddha hall for perpetual offerings. Hereafter...
Having completed three years of service, he and his colleagues, Official Yuan Zhen of the Judicial Office and Di-gong, purchased a boat to cross the sea and return to their hometown.

The military aide’s family stayed in the forward hold, while the judicial official stayed in the rear hold. When they reached the border of Shaoxing Prefecture, they were suddenly struck by a violent storm;
darkness fell on all four sides, and everyone was seized with terror. Suddenly, they saw ghosts within the sea...
The deity split the boat in two. Guo Sicheng’s former cargo was carried forward; with the wind and sails favorable, he went straight to the shore.
As for the Judicial Officer’s later boat, its people and luggage were all drowned in the sea.

This was because the Judicial Officer, in his administration of affairs, yielded to private interests and twisted the crooked to make it straight, thereby inviting this retribution. Military Commissioner Guo, however, maintained a virtuous heart and served the public with integrity.

Through the Dharma and his vow to save sentient beings, and further sustained by the power of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*, he was rescued and protected; he recovered and returned to his hometown.
The retribution for good and evil was as clear as pointing at one's palm. Among those who saw or heard of this, there were none who did not express deep admiration.
Zhao Bi was a scholar from Sizhou. He had traveled to the capital to take the imperial examinations when his wife passed away.

Later, after Zhao Bi had passed the exams and was returning home, he was about ten li from his house when, in a state between dream and reality, he saw his deceased wife by the roadside, her lamentations most earnest and piteous.
It was said: During her lifetime, Niannu had taken the lives of sentient beings; every time the crabs emerged, she would purchase them to make "drunken crabs" and eat them to her heart's content.
After her death, by the decree of King Yama, she was driven into the Crab Mountain, where she was seized by swarms of crabs that pincered out her eyes and caused blood to flow from her entire body.
She suffered thus day and night. Furthermore, during her life, she had not acted in accordance with the Dharma...
The dregs of vomited wine and the residue remaining in the bottom of the cup accumulate in the underworld to the amount of five *shi*, nine *dou*, seven *sheng*, and five *he*.
This causes the slave’s lifespan in the world of the living to be reduced by one *ji* (twelve years), and he further undergoes the suffering of the Great Hell for twenty-one days.

Furthermore, in accordance with the King’s decree, if the hell officials and jailers sell wine to the slave while awaiting the arrival of the Unconstant Ghosts (*mùcháng guǐ*) to summon his deceased soul, they shall all be hauled before the court.
I purchased wine and drew blood from my own body to pay for it, ensuring that every measure was repaid in full so as not to incur further suffering in the hells.
Now, hearing that my husband has passed the imperial examinations and is returning in glory, I have come specifically to plead with you.

The underworld authorities deeply respect those who transcribe the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*; I beg you to sell the dowry from my chamber and, with the proceeds, have this sūtra written for me.
She obtained seven fascicles. Relying on the merit of this *Prajñāpāramitā*, she could truly be delivered from the sufferings of hell. Her husband consented;
as soon as they arrived home, he immediately gave away his wealth to commission monks to copy the scripture.
When only two fascicles had been completed, one day he prepared the ritual offerings to visit his wife’s grave. Just as evening approached, he suddenly saw an old man who said, "I am a minor deity."
"Landowner, because your wife has taken up the merit of copying the sutras, she ascended to the celestial realms at noon yesterday, by order of King Yama, and is no longer seen beneath the earth.
Have you not seen the *Text on Abstinence from Killing* by Chan Master Foyin, which says:
'The various species of scales, shells, feathers, and fur—the minds of these sentient beings and the Buddha are no different. It is only because they misapplied their minds at that time.'"
This causes their heads and horns to differ from those of this life. They swim in the water and frolic in the forest; how can one bear to bring them here to provide for daily sustenance?
They are sharpened on blades, boiled over fires, or ground into paste. Unable to speak, they can only stare with their eyes; some are struck with hammers, others pierced with knives.

Dragged into the cauldrons of boiling brine, how truly terrifying! Their feathers and fur are singed away, their scales are scraped clean; though their backs are pared and their hearts gouged out, they still breathe hot sighs.
They praise the food in your throat, boasting of its fine flavor; they urge their sons and wives with clever words.

Knowing only how to indulge their natures and give rein to ignorance, they do not fear that the Offices of the Underworld record even a hair’s breadth of their deeds. As soon as life ends, karmic retribution arrives; facing King Yama in person, who would dare—?
The Name. Report it from beginning to end, one by one, without error. Where can you avoid the glowing embers and the boiling cauldrons?

I urge the worthy and noble: you must observe the prohibitions. Do not treat sentient beings as something trivial. For every morsel you eat of them, they shall return it to you. The words of the ancient sages are never false.
If you abstain from killing and can even purchase the release of life, you will avoid entering the Avīci Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering. Furthermore, *Man-t'ing-fang* (Full Court Fragrance).
Verse: How many scales and shells! How countless feathers and fur! Once awakened to the Buddha-nature, one is identical to all worldly people.

Why then do you stubbornly accept the "fatty" [meat] in your mouth? You painfully wield the butcher’s knife upon sentient beings; heads turn as fresh blood flies red, minced and roasted until shattered. I cannot bear to look upon them.
Just as I swallow it down my throat, the dragon’s liver and phoenix’s marrow ultimately leave no trace—nothing but delusion.
It is won. During one's life, premature death and many misfortunes abound. I exhort all people of the world to awaken and reflect: do not indulge your whims and provoke the Lord of Yama.
The original face of saṃsāra can be transformed in the blink of an eye.
The daughter of Li Xuanzong of Jiangling County in Jingzhou was thirteen years old when she dreamed of a *bhikṣu*.
The monk said to her, "You possess roots of goodness; why do you not recite the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*? He further said, "If there should be anyone in the world..."
Whether man or woman, if one can recite one fascicle daily with a pure mind, one’s lifespan will be increased in the world of the living;
when the hundred-year life comes to an end, one will immediately be reborn in the celestial realms. If one can thoroughly master the Prajñāpāramitā, one shall surely reach the other shore of Nirvāṇa.

Furthermore, if there are those who read this scripture, even if they have not yet completed it, upon death they will enter the underworld (Yin-fu) but will not be subject to its constraints or records; they shall instead be judged to be born into wealth and nobility.
The family received various excellent rewards. A daughter of the imperial court, following the instructions of a monk, recited three fascicles daily.
At the age of twenty-four, she had no desire for marriage. Suddenly, she contracted a severe fever (sāṃnipātaka) and died after three days.
Two messengers led her to an audience with King Yama. Upon investigation, the King found that the girl was without fault; furthermore, he saw a Buddha manifest upon the woman’s head. The King—
The King said, "Since this woman possesses the merit of Prajñā, I decree that her soul be restored. As he was about to release her, the King instructed her:

"Your father has enemies; therefore, upon returning to the world of the living, his lifespan shall first be reduced by two *ji* (twenty-four years). Before long, he shall be summoned to the Netherworld to face the evidence.
Because your father was fond of slicing raw fish for sashimi, there are now more than seven thousand fish who have filed a formal complaint against him."
"Seeking my life! If you do not believe me, return to the world of the living and ask your father; every night he dreams that he has fallen into a net, and he suffers from a headache every day.
This is the fish seeking retribution. The daughter regained her spirit and reported the matters of the underworld to her father one by one.
Upon hearing this, the father was struck with such terror and confusion that he knew not what to do. He then went together with his daughter to the Great Buddha Hall of Tianning Temple.
He provided a vegetarian feast for one hundred monks and made a vow to abstain from meat and wine. He personally transcribed forty-nine fascicles of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Once the transcription was complete, Emperor Xuanzong suddenly saw in a dream one night several hundred youths dressed in blue garments.
They all prostrated before the Emperor, declaring: "In days of yore, we were slaughtered by you. We each passed through the underworld to lodge our grievances and demand your life.
Now, by virtue of the merit of copying this scripture, we have all benefited from these wholesome powers;

we have escaped the suffering realms of the three evil paths and each attained rebirth in a good destination. Since you have now released us from our grievances, the underworld authorities shall restore your original lifespan. Furthermore—

May his longevity be extended. When the Emperor Xuan heard of this, he was filled with boundless joy. From that time forth, he recited the scriptures without ceasing and never abandoned his practice of goodness.
He reached the age of one hundred and twenty years; without illness, he requested a bath and passed away. (Recorded in the *Zazu ji*).

Wang Digong was a County Magistrate (Xianwei). He delighted in falconry and hunting, taking pleasure in killing and harming sentient beings. His wife remained at home, reciting the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* daily.
One day, while his wife was intently reciting the sutra, she saw her husband returning from a hunt. His wife earnestly exhorted her husband.
From the Fifteenth Section on the Merit of Upholding the Sūtra: Di Gong shared this same aspiration, yet he was unwilling to complete the entire scroll.
Instead, he entered the kitchen to slaughter living beings for cooking and feasted to his heart's content. Five years later, Di Gong suddenly suffered a stroke and lay bedridden;
though a year passed, he did not recover. One day, he saw two messengers come to summon him, and his life ended. Only...
With resentment in his heart, the two messengers led him to an audience with King Yama. The King rebuked Digu Gong in anger, saying:

"Since you have received rank and emolument, why did you not cultivate merit upon your existing fortune? Instead, you delighted in killing living beings. Your lifespan has been diminished and your provisions cut off;
I shall order the jailers to drive you into the cauldron of boiling water. The ghost-officials consulted their registers and reported to the King: "Although this man has committed killing..."
His karma was such that his good records were as heavy as a mountain. During his lifetime, he had once been urged by his wife to recite one section of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Although the merit was but a fragment of paper, it was as weighty as a register of evil deeds; thus, he should be exempted from punishment and released back to the world of the living.
Heaven issued an imperial decree: "Take a ladle of boiling broth from within the cauldron and pour it over his back; only then shall he be released. Consequently, he was restored to life once more.
Later, he suffered from a carbuncle on his back that spread until his entire body was festering and rotting; the pain was unbearable, and no medicine could cure it.
One day, he instructed his wife to go before the Buddha and make a vow on his behalf, saying: "From this day forth, I swear never to kill living beings.

Once my illness has healed, I vow to personally transcribe the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* and, maintaining a vegetarian fast, uphold its teachings. Suddenly, one night, he saw a monk in a dream who stroked him with his hand.
Digong circumambulated it three times. When dawn came, he looked at the abscess and found it had already healed, leaving no scar or mark behind.
Such is the retribution for good and evil (from the *Baoying ji*).
Court Censor Feng daily recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* in three fascicles.
When he was twenty-eight years old, one day, on account of state affairs, he prepared a memorial and presented it to the Emperor. That very night at the fourth watch, he suddenly saw two messengers.

He was escorted into the underworld and presented before the Celestial Son Yama. The deity issued a decree, saying: "Your lifespan was destined to reach seventy-nine years, and your rank was to reach the Council of State.
However, because of your memorial petition, you have brought harm to the state and the people; therefore, your emoluments shall be cut off and your life-span subtracted. Feng was struck with terror.
Prostrating himself, he addressed [the King], saying: "Since my allotted lifespan has not yet expired, I beg for the gift of rebirth.

I vow to uphold the scriptures for the rest of my life, constantly practicing meritorious deeds and refraining from committing sins or transgressions against the celestial laws. The King, pitying his turning of heart toward goodness, released him back into the world of the living.
He admonished him repeatedly, saying: "Whenever you hold authority over governance, you must prepare a register. During the day, you shall..."
One must record one's deeds at night. If they cannot be recorded, they must certainly not have been performed; this is the method for extending one’s years.

If one performs even a single act of goodness—focusing on relieving the people and showing compassion toward all things—one’s blessings and lifespan will increase. However, if one employs a heart of exploitation and oppression, the Supreme Deity detests it, and thus one’s life is shortened and one’s merit is diminished.
Feng was granted rebirth because he daily practiced expedient means, benefiting the state and bestowing upon the people through hidden virtue (*yin-de*).
His fame spread daily, and his life span reached ninety-eight years. He was appointed as Chancellor.
One day, while lying ill, his ninth son, who was then eleven years old, came out from the hall to play. He saw countless hell-wardens with ox-heads and horse-faces.
The son asked the ghosts, "For what reason have you come here? The ghost officials replied, "We have come specifically to welcome [you] to the Yama Heaven."
The son was struck with alarm and wept as he entered the hall, reporting what he had seen to his father.

The father laughed heartily and clapped his hands, saying, "To be a Grand Minister of State while alive and to become King Yama after death—this is my true vocation. He spoke in verse: "Cease using the lead pen to flaunt your literary skill;

Turn instead to the King of Emptiness and joyfully leave the household life. Having already resolved with single-minded devotion to return to the Great Way, [Do not seek fame through worldly writings.]”

One must endure the bitter obstruction of the six thieves; though they urge one toward the company of wife and concubines, it ultimately leads to illness. A position as high as that of a Duke or Minister is like a flower;
from this point on, in his final years, he relied upon the sword of wisdom. He wished to entrust his name to Danxia.

He requested a bath, changed into his court robes, and sat in meditation until his passing. He further composed a verse: "Beating the drum within the vast ocean, Hearing the bell atop Mount Sumeru. The Mirror of Karma..."
Come! Shatter it and turn back; penetrate through into empty space.
Student Jiang of Zhou—Student Jiang of the village—died suddenly at the age of twenty-three. He saw two messengers pursuing him.
The soul was led before the Son of Heaven, Yama. He issued a decree, saying: "In your previous life you cultivated merit, which has granted you a lifespan of eighty-two years in this life.
You passed the examination in the Dingchou year and rose to the rank of high official. It was not right for you to kill oxen and eat their meat; you have violated the Celestial Law.
In accordance with the Decree of the Jade Emperor, I order that your allotted years be reduced and your emoluments cut off. Since you were a scholar, how could you—"
I have not heard that in Haizhou there was thunder and rain for seven days and seven nights, nor that the heavens sent down a stone drum inscribed with these words:
"The myriad things are created solely by the mind; the ox suffers the greatest bitterness. Behold those who die a violent death—they are all people who ate oxen.
Formerly, there was a Jinshi named Yu Xin, who killed oxen to eat their meat. Relying on his literary talent and cleverness, he slandered the Triple Gem. After his death, he underwent [retribution].

The various hell-beings have now been transformed into tortoises. The King issued a command for the ghost-officials to lead the tortoises to the foot of the hall and ordered Master Jiang to examine them.
The tortoises had nine heads, and from the eyes of each head blood was flowing; their suffering was incessant. These were none other than the Yu Xins.
One ghost-official said to Master Jiang, "You must urgently inform the Son of Heaven to reform his evils and cultivate goodness. We beg of you..."
He was granted his life back. [The officer] said, "If it were judged that you enter hell, there would be no time of release. Sengsheng asked, "What path is there? I pray you will instruct me.
The ghost official said, "In the underworld, we hold in deep reverence the copying and upholding of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and the *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*.
If you resolve to do so, you shall immediately obtain liberation. Having received this instruction, he reported it to the Son of Heaven.
He said: "I reflect that my parents have grown old and there are no other brothers to attend to them as they live out their lives.
Being young, I was ignorant of sin and merit, leading me to commit grave offenses. Although I have read the literary works of Yu Xin, I have never slandered the Buddha or the Sangha.

Since my allotted lifespan has not yet ended, I beg to be granted permission to return to the world of the living, so that I may filially support my parents and make a vow to transcribe the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*."
He devoted himself to the *Lotus Sūtra* and the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, maintaining a vegetarian diet for the remainder of his life and diligently upholding them.

The Son of Heaven, taking pity on his transformation of heart—having turned away from evil and followed the good—reprimanded him, released him, and restored his soul. The Son of Heaven admonished him, saying:

"When you return to the world of the living, support your parents with filial piety, revere the Triple Gem, recite and uphold the scriptures, and cultivate wholesome deeds. If you should violate these again, [you shall suffer the consequences]."

He entered the Yellow Springs; even if a thousand Buddhas were to appear in the world, there would be no way for him to repent. Once Student Jiang had regained his life, his relatives, acquaintances, and neighbors all came to inquire about the circumstances of his return;
there was not one who did not feel shame and remorse, reforming their ways and starting anew.
Military Aide Huo was reciting the Diamond Sutra when he suddenly saw the ground beneath the hall crack open, and Bao Longtu surged forth from within.

He declared, "I am the Officer of Swift Reporting. The Military Aide asked the Officer of Swift Reporting, "You report evil but do not report good; how can those who are good suffer [the consequences]?"

The hungry and cold suffer; the wicked are provided with abundant clothing and food. Those who are pure find it difficult to pass their days, while those who are turbid enjoy much prosperity and change.

The filial and obedient endure much hardship, yet those who commit the five heinous crimes are met with affectionate regard. Whether the officials of swift retribution are efficacious or not, whether they manifest themselves or not—this depends solely upon [the nature of one's deeds].

Since the spirits must manifest their numinous power, and since they have appeared, they must teach what has been manifested. I pray you grant me one clear word, so as to spare the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa from resentment.
Bao Longtu replied: "I preside over the Office of Swift Retribution. It is not that I do not report the wicked; it is not that I do not report the virtuous.

The virtuous may suffer temporary poverty, while the wicked may enjoy provisional satiety and warmth. As for those who are turbid, rebellious, crooked, and evil, their cases shall be fully adjudicated."

Excerpts of Names. First, the name and surname; second, the removal of deities of fortune and rank; third, the severing of the lineage for future generations; fourth, the dispatching of calamitous stars to descend;
fifth, causing a deranged mind to devise [evil]; sixth, being befriended by wicked people; seventh, requiring a short lifespan; eighth, being beset by illness;
ninth, encountering the perils of water and fire; tenth, being punished by royal law. These ten hardships are all [the results of] these ten [karmic causes].
"Evil person! Military Aide, do not question me. This mirror is most clear; one day, when heaven and earth behold it, ten thousand blessings shall descend all at once.
The poem says: "The profound blue sky cannot be deceived; even before an intention is raised, it already knows.
Good and evil will ultimately receive their retribution; there is only a contest between what comes sooner and what comes later."
Commander Huo questioned the Office of Rapid Reporting once more: "In the world of the living, there are monks, nuns, virtuous friends, officials, and commoners.
Among them are those who uphold the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. When their hundred-year lifespan comes to an end and they die to enter the realm of darkness, what will become of them?"
"Can one transcend [rebirth]? Bao Longtu replied, "It can be attained.
Zhang Yin was then in his early twenties; he maintained a vegetarian diet and regularly recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. There was also a butcher in the same village named...
Zhang Yin had slaughtered many pigs and sheep. Consequently, his grievances were lodged with the local courts and the provincial administration.

By order of King Yama, an emissary from the netherworld mistakenly summoned Zhang Yin, who was in possession of a scripture. The King rebuked him, saying, "During your life in the world, how could you have committed the slaughter of living beings?

Zhang Yin replied, "My primary occupation was the study of scriptures; I never engaged in butchery. The King then commanded that the *karmic mirror* be used to examine him, and indeed, [the evidence] appeared.

Regarding his roots of goodness, the Son of Heaven asked the ghost official, "How much of a lifespan should Zhang Yin be granted? The ghost official consulted the registers and found that his life would reach ninety years.
The Son of Heaven said to Yin, "Since you have never slaughtered living beings and furthermore maintain the sutras..."

Now you have been released and returned to life. At the time of your death, it was precisely midsummer; three weeks had already passed, and your corpse had rotted and decayed, no longer fit for re-entrance.
Later, he informed the King, saying: "Since your corpse is no longer fit for entrustment, command a messenger to urgently summon the butcher Zhang Yin to receive his retribution.
The King said to Zhang Yin, who held the sutra: "Your name is the same as that of the butcher."
They were of the same surname and born on the same year, month, day, and hour; it was appropriate that she should revive by relying upon that corpse.

When the butcher saw her husband return to consciousness three days after his death, he was overcome with joy and, paying no heed at all, ran straight back to his original dwelling. He spoke thus to his wife and son: [The rest of the narrative follows.]
I have been reborn once more; the butcher’s family recognizes me as their husband, while the family that recites the scriptures recognizes me as their father.

Both families dispute the matter, and who can distinguish the truth? Thereupon, the case was presented to the official, who clearly ruled in accordance with the Prefect’s judgment: "The body and the soul are born separately."
Their names were not different, yet at birth their lineages were distinct; now that they have died, they have returned to share the same vital essence.

Although his body belongs to a butcher’s family, his temperament and voice are those of one who upholds the sutras—it is truly difficult to distinguish between them. I respectfully propose that the two families take turns raising each child for one month.

He nevertheless submitted a truthful memorial to the imperial court regarding this rare occurrence, noting that the descendants of the butcher’s family had reformed their ways and turned toward goodness.
Xu Ji was a local official from Hangzhou who would every night at the fifth watch recite three fascicles of the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* until they were completed.
He was just entering the official gate when it became known that his family was wealthy. One day, more than a hundred bandits entered Xu Ji’s house;
they bound up all the adults and children together and tied Xu Ji himself to an archery target. Xu Ji said, "The indestructible body of the Vajra—what shall I do now?
In an instant, he saw a Buddha appear in the sky, and his fear was somewhat relieved. The bandits...
They all released arrows to shoot at him, firing a hundred shafts in succession. Some struck the target and fell to the ground, yet neither the body nor the head of Sengqi was wounded in the least.
The bandits were struck with terror and asked Sengqi, "What sorcery do you possess? He replied, "I have no sorcery.

Every day I have single-mindedly received and upheld the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, visualizing that the Triple Gem and the dragon deities provide protection; this is the resulting response."
The bandits joined their palms in reverence and, realizing their error with alarm, released them all at once.
As for Old Lu:
he was a butcher from south of the city of Huzhou. When he was twenty-three years old, he saw a wandering mendicant before his gate.
The monk said, "Mimi, you have taught and transformed those with whom you have a karmic connection. Lu, do you not understand this? Lu did not comprehend his meaning.
The monk said, "You have slaughtered pigs and sheep countless times; why do you not change your profession? Lu said, "I inherit my ancestral occupation and cannot bear to abandon it.

The monk said, "If you do not change, in future lives you will surely fall into this same category and be killed by others. Vengeance will follow vengeance, with no end in sight. It is a life of poverty..."
The Sangha observes that you possess roots of goodness from past lives; why do you not uphold the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* and the *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*?
If you were to uphold them, your evil karma would be eliminated and your wholesome merit would increase.
Have you not seen how Emperor Renzong personally praised the Lotus Sutra, saying: "Its sixty thousand words and seven fascicles contain boundless wondrous meanings within"?
The ambrosia of overflowing joy is contained within, moistening and irrigating the crown of the head from time to time;

drops of the finest cream (paramārtha-ghṛta) flow coolly from the edges of his white jade-like teeth, while rays of light emanate from the red lotus of his tongue. Even if one has committed sins as vast as a mountain range, they are extinguished by just two or three lines of the wondrous Dharma.
When the monk finished speaking, he turned his head and was no longer seen. Lu then attained awakening, thinking it must have been the Buddha and Avalokiteśvara.
The Bodhisattva Guanshiyin manifested an emanation body to come and exhort me. I immediately invited an artisan to paint a single scroll depicting the images of Amitābha Buddha, Guanyin, and Shizhi.
I prepared a feast for offerings and began studying under a teacher to recite the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* and the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Before five years had passed, I was able to recite them from memory. Furthermore, it was as if I had slaughtered a pig yesterday and [the consequences] were manifest today.

As for the number of sheep [to be slaughtered], he personally approached the Buddha before the night began, burning incense and reciting one copy of the Lotus Sūtra and seventeen fascicles of the Diamond Sūtra.
Facing the Buddha, he performed repentance, declaring aloud: "Tomorrow morning, I shall slaughter several pigs and sheep.

I vow that through the merit of reading these scriptures, may the pigs and sheep being killed be delivered; may they exhaust this retributive body and be born early in the Pure Land. May my own life..."

At the time of his end, he was spared from this karmic retribution. His complexion became like that of the morning sun, and Lu felt his body grow light and his strength restored; he found joy within himself.

He reached the age of eighty-one. Half a month before his death, he invited all his relatives, friends, market neighbors, and local residents, announcing that he would pass away on the ninth day of the eleventh month. On that day, he prepared a simple meal of vegetables.

They welcomed him with formal ceremony and parted with mutual farewells. When the appointed time arrived, they all went together; once the meal was finished, he indeed requested a bath and changed his robes, sitting upright until he passed away.

Among the local officials and friends from his hometown, there were none who did not gaze upon him in reverence and offer words of praise. At that time, Zhou Jing witnessed it personally and likewise accompanied them in seeing him off.
The Verse says: How truly marvelous is this old man of the land living in the world! His children and grandchildren embroider him with affection, their smiles filling his cheeks.
Eighty-one years have passed like waking from a dream; Among the hundreds of thousands of samādhis, all doubt and suspicion have ceased.

Killing does not obstruct the nature of True Suchness (Tathatā); Reciting the Buddha’s name first empties the heap of sins and merits. Moved by this, the Compassionate Honored One comes to welcome and guide him; Within the Crystal Palace, white lotuses bloom. The Verse.
He said: "For over sixty years I was solely devoted to the karma of killing; with knife and scale in hand, I practiced in secret.
This morning I have found the path to Bodhi—a lotus flower blooming within the water and amidst the fire."
